title: US Refiners Are Making the Most Fuel Since Pre-Covid
summary: US refiners are turning crude oil into products like gasoline and diesel at a pace not seen since before the Covid-19 pandemic, but even that is unlikely to rein in soaring prices soon amid a historic fuel crunch.

title: From Food to Football: How Clouse Came to the Commanders
summary: Washington Commanders President Mark Clouse talks about why he left the Campbell's Company as CEO to take this job. He speaks to Bloomberg's Randall Williams at a Newsmakers event in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can We Trust Election Prediction Markets?
summary: Leading prediction markets have been heralded as “truth machines” — arenas for mass betting that reveal what people really think when they’ve got money on the line. But a new Bloomberg investigation has found evidence that these markets are vulnerable to manipulation. On today’s Big Take podcast, host Sarah Holder and Bloomberg investigative reporter Liam Vaughan dig into what can happen when prediction markets mix with politics.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Fall as 30-Year Bond Yields Surge After Fed: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks ended sharply lower as concerns about inflation drove longer-dated bond yields to an almost two-decade high after the Federal Reserve left rates steady despite a resurgence in oil prices.

title: Nothing Nefarious With 'Circle Financing': Dorrell
summary:
Mike Dorrell, chairman CEO and co-founder, Stonepeak joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Nvidia is working on a fresh round of AI deals worth more than $750 billion, accelerating investments that skeptics have warned are artificially inflating demand and valuations across the industry. Such transactions have left many AI companies increasingly intertwined, potentially exposing the sector to systemic shocks.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Binance.US Wants to Join Prediction Markets Race With CFTC Stamp
summary: Binance.US is planning to apply for a license with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission that would help it start its own prediction market, the company’s chief executive officer said at a conference on Wednesday.

title: Ford Hikes Outlook on Strong SUV Demand
summary: Ford shares rose after the automaker boosted its profit outlook for the second time this year, driven by robust consumer demand for high-margin SUVs. Bloomberg’s Keith Naughton reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: FIFA Working On Plan To Raise As Much As $4.2B
summary:
Bloomberg's Vanessa Perdomo joins Dani Burger and Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." when FIFA announced controversial plans to raise external investment of $4.2 billion. In response to the proposal, UEFA, the organizer of European football, reacted furiously and saying it's considering a boycott of FIFA events. Also a top EU official saying today the FIFA proposal may spark competition law concerns.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Emerging-Market Currencies Climb as Fed Holds Rates Steady
summary: Emerging-market currencies gained on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, pushing the US dollar lower following mounting speculation that policymakers would use this meeting to tighten monetary policy.

title: Gold Trims Gain as Fed Holds Rates, Signals Hike Support
summary: Gold pared gains after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged as expected, while signaling that support for higher borrowing costs is growing as officials assess the inflationary impact of the Iran war.

title: Investment Committee: Consumer Brands & Spending Habits
summary: Enna Weng, head of capital markets at China Renaissance Global Markets, Eva Davis, managing partner, external affairs at Winston Taylor, and Tricia Glynn, managing partner at Advent International, join Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apollo's Slok Says Warsh Silence Fuels Treasury Selloff
summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's decision to abandon forward guidance on monetary policy is driving bond market volatility, with 30-year Treasuries selling off after Wednesday's rate decision, according to Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management. He speaks on Bloomberg Television's "The Fed Decides." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apollo’s Slok Says Fed’s New Silence Fuels ‘Yo-Yo’ Bond Market
summary: Apollo Global Management’s Torsten Slok said the Federal Reserve’s abandonment of forward guidance is fueling historic bond market volatility, sending Treasury yields swinging “up and down like a yo-yo.”

title: Thoma Bravo Cedes to Lender Revolt on $5 Billion Proofpoint Loan
summary: Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint Inc. has reworked a $5 billion loan deal, offering major concessions to lenders increasingly anxious about AI-driven tech disruption.

title: Earnings Reflect Changing Consumer Priorities
summary: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Despite being less than halfway through earnings seasons, and with retailers yet to report, many consumer-facing companies have announced results that make it clear inflation is changing spending patterns. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Warsh Says Fed Won't Be Constrained by Market Prices
summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says markets can be a good source of information but not a determinative or perfect source during a news conference following the central bank's decision to leave rates unchanged. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Dollar Sinks Most in Two Weeks After Fed Holds Rates Steady
summary: The dollar fell the most in two weeks after the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, and as traders pared bets that the central bank will boost borrowing costs at its next meeting in September.

title: Jersey Mike’s Set To Make Trading Debut Thursday
summary: Bloomberg's Ryan Gould joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Jersey Mike’s Subs’s initial public offering has attracted investor demand for more than 10 times the available shares ahead of pricing on Wednesday, according to people familiar with the matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Koch Said to Mull $15B Sale of Edged
summary: Bloomberg's Allison McNeely joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Koch is exploring a sale of Edged, the data center developer it cofounded to build projects for the biggest hyperscalers, according to people with knowledge of the matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nasdaq 100 Enters Correction, S&P 500 Falls After Fed Decision
summary: The Nasdaq 100 Index closed in correction territory, pushing the broader stock market lower as the Federal Reserve refrained from raising interest rates but a trio of dissents signaled support for tighter monetary policy.
